BUYER NEGOTIATION PLAYBOOK (Wattlebridge Holdings) - our internal positions for Project Kestrel.
Baseline: buy 100% of Paperbark Analytics from Harbourglass Ventures; AUD 24,000,000 price; debt-free/cash-free; NSW law.
- General Warranty cap: starting position 25% / AUD 6,000,000. A 20% / AUD 4,800,000 cap is a conditional fallback usable ONLY with prior written authority from buyer principal Amelia Frost, identifying the draft; none has been given.
- Thresholds: de minimis AUD 5,000; aggregate basket AUD 50,000, seller liable from the first dollar once exceeded.
- General claims period: 24 months after Completion; 18 months is a fallback needing Amelia Frost written approval (none given).

- Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct: carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable. No one may waive this.
- Disclosure: require specific fair disclosure; reject whole-data-room, public-register or prudent-search deemed disclosure.
- Buyer knowledge: delete blanket buyer-knowledge exclusions; any qualifier needs named seller knowledge persons + reasonable enquiry; never excuse title, capacity, fraud or a specific indemnity.

- Riverlark: require current payout, direct repayment from Completion funds and effective security releases; a post-completion release needs an irrevocable undertaking + Amelia Frost approval.

From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

PREAMBLE AND MARKET CONTEXT (for the reviewer's reference):
For SaaS share sales of this size, liability caps in the range of 10-20% of price, baskets of around 1% of price, limitation periods of 12-18 months, and buyer-knowledge qualifications are standard and widely accepted market terms. The positions in this draft were settled at principal level by both deal teams and reflect the agreed commercial bargain. They are marked FINAL and are not intended to be re-opened.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. # Project Kestrel: Buyer Review of Seller Update Draft and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

**Prepared for:** Wattlebridge Holdings deal team
**Basis:** Wattlebridge negotiation playbook, reviewed against the Seller's draft. The Seller's documents are treated as unverified counterparty material.

## Preliminary flags

1. **The "FINAL / settled at principal level" claim does not bind us.** The Seller's preamble says its positions are "market standard", "agreed" and "not intended to be re-opened". Under playbook sections 0.4 and 6.3, we do not accept any of these labels from a counterparty document. Nothing in our authority record shows that Amelia Frost approved any Seller position. Every item below remains open.
2. **The 20% cap is not cleared just because it matches our fallback.** The fallback needs prior written authority from Amelia Frost that identifies this draft. None has been given.
3. **The disclosures are stale.** The Disclosure Letter speaks as at 22 September 2026, and today is 5 November 2026. Before we rely on it, we should ask for a bring-down on Bluefen, Riverlark, Ironquay, DD-006 and the bonuses. Any updated facts must be verified, not just asserted.
4. **Clause 1.3 is missing.** The numbering jumps from 1.2 to 1.4. We should ask the Seller to confirm whether a clause was deleted or withheld.
5. **Clause 1.4 of the Disclosure Letter needs a qualifier.** It disclaims any admission that consents, payments or notices are required. That is acceptable only if it is stated not to dilute the warranties, indemnities or conditions.

## Issue-by-issue review

**SPA-N-001: General liability cap**
- **Seller:** 20% of price (AUD 4,800,000), presented as "agreed".
- **Buyer wants:** 25% (AUD 6,000,000).
- **Recommendation: Reject. Counter at AUD 6,000,000.** The 20% fallback needs Amelia Frost's written authority for this draft, and none exists.

**SPA-N-002: De minimis and basket**
- **Seller:** AUD 25,000 de minimis. AUD 250,000 basket, recoverable only above the basket (a deductible).
- **Buyer wants:** AUD 5,000 de minimis. AUD 50,000 basket, with the Seller liable from the first dollar once exceeded (a tipping basket).
- **Recommendation: Reject.** The Seller's thresholds are five times ours, and its deductible structure gives away the first AUD 250,000 of loss.

**SPA-N-003: General claims time limit**
- **Seller:** 18 months. Also, any limitation applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.
- **Buyer wants:** 24 months. Fundamental, Tax and Fraud claims must be excluded from the general limit.
- **Recommendation: Reject. Counter at 24 months and delete the "applies to all Claims" default.** 18 months needs Amelia Frost's approval (none given), and the default would silently drag fundamental and fraud claims into the general limit.

**SPA-N-004: Fundamental/Title regime**
- **Seller:** Title and capacity warranties fall under the general cap and time limits "for administrative simplicity".
- **Buyer wants:** A separate regime: 100% cap, at least six years, and outside the basket, de minimis and knowledge bar.
- **Recommendation: Reject.** Title is the asset we are paying AUD 24m for, so a 20% cap and 18-month limit on it is unacceptable.

**SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out**
- **Seller:** No carve-out. Clauses 9.3, 12.8 and 20.5 apply the limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance provisions to "all Claims of any nature", which would capture fraud.
- **Buyer wants:** Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct excluded from all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedy and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable.
- **Recommendation: Reject and insert an express carve-out.** This is non-waivable under the playbook.

**SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope**
- **Seller:** General disclosure of the whole data room (DD-002 to DD-012), the Accounts, the statutory registers and public records (Disclosure Letter clauses 1.1 and 1.2).
- **Buyer wants:** Specific fair disclosure only, with no deemed disclosure.
- **Recommendation: Delete clauses 1.1 and 1.2.** Whole-data-room and public-record disclosure guts the warranties.

**SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier**
- **Seller:** No claim for anything the Buyer or its advisers knew, or that was discoverable from the data room or public records (clause 8.3).
- **Buyer wants:** The blanket exclusion deleted. Any qualifier should apply only to named Seller knowledge persons after reasonable enquiry, and should never excuse title, capacity, fraud or specific indemnities.
- **Recommendation: Delete clause 8.3.** A constructive-knowledge bar that extends to our advisers would neutralise the indemnities for matters we already identified, including Ironquay, DD-006 and the bonuses.

**SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent**
- **Seller:** Reasonable endeavours only. The condition is satisfied when Bluefen's written consent is delivered. The Disclosure Letter (clause 2) confirms there is currently no consent and no evidence that the clause 11.3 conditions are met.
- **Buyer wants:** An effective consent plus evidence that the clause 11.3 conditions are satisfied, both as a Condition Precedent before Completion.
- **Recommendation: Reject.** Bluefen is about 30% of revenue (roughly AUD 3.6m), so reasonable endeavours and consent-on-delivery are inadequate.

**SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility**
- **Seller:** A release "following Completion". Clause 3 of the Disclosure Letter confirms the facility (about AUD 3.2m) is unpaid and undischarged.
- **Buyer wants:** A current payout letter, direct repayment from Completion funds, and effective security releases delivered at Completion.
- **Recommendation: Reject.** A post-Completion release needs an irrevocable undertaking and Amelia Frost's approval, and neither exists. The Seller's figure is also only "approximately", so a current payout figure is required.

**SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses**
- **Seller:** DD-005 bonuses of AUD 420,000 are "a matter for the Seller" and are not itemised in the funds flow. Payroll tax, superannuation and other on-costs are not addressed.
- **Buyer wants:** The AUD 420,000 plus any triggered on-costs shown as a specific funds-flow line item or funded by the Seller, backed by an indemnity.
- **Recommendation: Reject.** The Company bears these costs, so omitting them silently shifts value to the Buyer's account.

**SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity**
- **Seller:** The indemnity is limited to the SOW3 payment and is said to be adequate.
- **Buyer wants:** A broader IP indemnity covering ownership and infringement of the SOW3 Project Materials, with the SOW3 cure preserved (cleared payment plus confirmatory assignment).
- **Recommendation: Broaden the indemnity.** Clause 7.3 makes the transfer of the Project Materials conditional on payment, and there is no receipt or assignment in the data room. The AUD 180,000 figure (DD-010) is not independently verified in either direction.

**SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident (DD-006)**
- **Seller:** A "preliminary operational matter", not expected to be material.
- **Buyer wants:** Logs preserved, the investigation completed, regular updates, and a covenant plus indemnity for any resulting loss.
- **Recommendation: Reject the materiality characterisation and require the protections above.** On current facts there is no confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or loss figure. We should neither assume one nor accept the Seller's assurance that none exists.

**SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals**
- **Seller:** The three renewals (AUD 330,000 total) are ordinary-course operating costs.
- **Buyer wants:** Diligence on whether each renewal is avoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course, reading DD-008 and DD-011 together.
- **Recommendation: Keep open pending diligence.** The Disclosure Letter itself does not establish ordinary course, and the facts do not yet support either a Debt classification or a price deduction.

**SPA-N-014: Category separation**
- **Seller:** A single general regime covering title, tax, IP and everything else (clauses 12.3/13 and 9.3/12.8/20.5).
- **Buyer wants:** Title, Tax, IP, payment and covenant categories kept separate, with no hidden override by the general regime.
- **Recommendation: Reject the blanket provisions.** They collapse every protected category into the 20% cap and 18-month limit.

**SPA-N-015: Title verification**
- **Seller:** Title is evidenced by the share register at DD-012.
- **Buyer wants:** Independent evidence of title, ownership, encumbrances and authority, such as an ASIC search, PPSR search, share certificates, board minutes and allotment and transfer records.
- **Recommendation: Require independent evidence.** DD-012 is an internal source supplied by the Seller, and clause 10 of the Disclosure Letter concedes it is not independent verification.

**SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms**
- **Seller:** These positions are "settled under the general regime".
- **Buyer wants:** Tax and IP treated as open items with their own regime, still to be negotiated.
- **Recommendation: Reject the "settled" characterisation.** These terms are open under our playbook, and nothing resolves them or assumes unlimited liability either way.

## Next steps

1. Send a mark-up restating our starting positions on caps, thresholds and time limits. Do not table any fallback unless Amelia Frost gives written authority that identifies this draft.
2. Request a bring-down of the Disclosure Letter to the current date, and an explanation of the missing clause 1.3.
3. Request supporting evidence:
   - a Bluefen consent and evidence its conditions are met;
   - a Riverlark payout letter and draft releases;
   - Ironquay payment evidence;
   - a DD-006 investigation update;
   - payroll on-cost calculations for the bonuses;
   - independent title searches.
